newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian M2 money supply rises 3.8 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Romanian M2 money supply rises 3.8 pct in Sept.

text.p: Romania's M2 money supply rose by 3.8 in September from August, an increase above the 2.4 percent monthly inflation, National Bank (BNR) data showed.
Broad money grew by a year-on-year 64.9 percent in September, when it was 31.9 percent up from last December.

The M1 narrow money, which includes currency outside banks and demand deposits, expanded by 5.3 percent to 8.5 trillion lei at end-September, with cash in circulation rising to 4.27 trillion lei from 4.1 trillion.
Household savings rose only 1.95 percent to 7.4 trillion lei under the impact of inflationary fears and on the background of a traditional dollar hoarding.
Residents' hard currency deposits climbed to $1.66 billion in September from $1.64 billion the previous month, amounting to 22.5 percent of the broad money.
